thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-cluster-prod queue depth > 10k for > 3m; 90th latency spike, sustained 429s observed. region=us-west2 pools=gpuhotpath,hotpool

pagerduty-bot: PAGER: maria assigned (oncall) — escalation policy: gpu-oncall

maria (oncall): on it. ack. starting triage. any customer-facing outages?

sam (sre): seeing 5xxs -> mostly 429s, appears during autoscale ramp. queue depth graph: https://grafana.redwood/shot/CLUSTER-QUEUE-WEST2 (brief)

leo (runtime): fwiw, we just landed rate-tier change last hour (canary) that modified token regeneration defaults. suspecting regen set too low for new burst pattern.

jing (infra): confirmed autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but limited by per-pool max and tokenwindow backpressure. snippet:

```

2026-03-15T10:02:15Z autoscaler: attempt_scale(pool=gpuhotpath) -> desired=24 current=12
2026-03-15T10:02:15Z ratepolicy: token_window_consumed(pool=gpuhotpath) -> avail=0 regen_rate=5/s limit=100
2026-03-15T10:02:16Z autoscaler: hold_scale(reason=tokenbucket-exhausted)
```

maria (oncall): okay, so autoscaler is trying but ratepolicy is gating it. Impact: some customer requests getting 429s and being enqueued; hitting SLOs. Need live mitigation asap.

sam (sre): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily relax token regen for gpuhotpath to 200/s; 2) raise pool max to allow immediate scale to desired=24; 3) open fallback route to fallback-model variant in us-east1 for non-enterprise tenants. doing step 1 now.

leo (runtime): who has permission to change ratepolicy? I can push a hotfix to runtime config, but infra will need to bump pool max.

jing (infra): I'll patch pool max. running command: `infractl pools update gpuhotpath --max-instances=32`

ops-bot: deploy started: infractl update, request_id=cli-8812

sam (sre): changing token regen in ratepolicy service: `POST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/admin/ratepolicies/gpuhotpath` body `{ "regen_per_sec": 200 }` — applying now.

incident-bot: NOTE: configuration change applied by sam at 10:07:12Z. 2m cooldown for policy to propagate.

maria (oncall): customer comm? I can draft a short note in status that we're seeing degraded throughput for some requests and working on mitigations.

leo (runtime): autoscaler observed new headroom after patch. logs:

```

2026-03-15T10:09:38Z ratepolicy: token_window_replenish(pool=gpuhotpath) -> regen=200/s avail=1340
2026-03-15T10:09:39Z autoscaler: scale_to(pool=gpuhotpath) -> new_desired=24 triggered_by=queue_depth
2026-03-15T10:10:05Z poolmgr: new_instance_attached id=gpu-ix-043 status=ready
```

sam (sre): seeing queue drain slowly. 429s dropped from ~15% -> ~3% in 7m. good but still a tail.

jing (infra): pool max updated to 32, autoscaler backfill in progress. infra health ok.

maria (oncall): good. mark oncall handoff in 30m? Also create a task to revert canary change and bake tests for token regen with new traffic shapes.

sam (sre): root cause hypothesis: canary rate-tier rollout accidentally changed default regen from 1500/s -> 5/s for pools without explicit override. combined with recent bursty usage pattern (prefetching + streaming clients) this starved token windows, which both blocked request acceptance and signalled autoscaler backoff.

leo (runtime): follow-ups: 1) add a safety floor for regen per-pool (min 50/s) 2) add alert for tokenwindow utilization > 80% for > 2m 3) add unit/integration test for rate-tier rollouts.

maria (oncall): I'm creating incident ticket INC-2026-318 in #postmortems and assigning to sam/leo/jing. I'll update customers via status page: "Partial throttling causing elevated 429s in us-west2; mitigation applied; recovery in progress."

ops-bot: incident ticket created INC-2026-318 by maria

sam (sre): temporary mitigation validated. next: patch the rollout job to not flip defaults for non-targeted pools and run canary against synthetic burst tests before rollout. I'll open PR and tag @leo @jing for review.

maria (oncall): thanks all. leaving note: oncall handoff scheduled at 11:00Z — whoever takes over, watch queue depth and tokenwindow graphs, and don't revert regen until pool fully drained and autoscaler stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: impact reduced. next update in 30m or on status change.
